title: DFT container week

notices: Ship 3 Howth Carrier was delayed leaving Greenock: it now arrives at hour 13 (planned berthing hour 4). Its planned departure stays hour 11.

title: Irish Sea ferries
blurb: A week of Irish Ferries, Stena Line and Liverpool RoRo calls. A late Ulysses, a channel gale, and an unscheduled freight ship. Slot times are illustrative.
notices: Ferry slot times in this scenario are illustrative, not an official timetable.
Irish Ferries may use berths 49 and 51A; Stena Line is planned on berth 51; the Alexandra Basin jetty (26 and 27) handles the Dublin–Liverpool RoRo service.
Ship 3 Ulysses (h41) was delayed leaving Holyhead: it now arrives at hour 46 (planned berthing hour 41). Its planned departure stays hour 43. The next Ulysses call still wants berth 49 at hour 53.

Gale notice: ships of 180 m and over may not berth or leave between hour 70 and hour 78 (southerly gale on the Liffey channel). A ship that finishes cargo inside the window waits alongside until it ends.
Unscheduled freight RoRo: ship 43 Cairnryan Freight (186 m) arrives at hour 74, needs 6 hours alongside and asks to sail by hour 86. It may use berths 26, 27 or 52.

title: Oil berths and tidal windows
blurb: Product, bitumen and LPG tankers on OB1–OB4. Deep draughts meet official approach depths only around high water. One late ship and one priority discharge.
notices: Deep product tankers (draught around 10 m) cannot transit the official 7.7–7.8 m approach at low water. The planner blocks berthing and departure outside the tidal window (approach depth + tide − 1.0 m UKC).
OB1 and OB2 take petroleum products; OB3 takes bitumen and LPG; OB4 is shallower (survey 6.2 m) and only suits the lighter bitumen calls.
Ship 5 Eastern Grade (h44) was delayed leaving Pembroke: it now arrives at hour 55 (planned berthing hour 44). Its planned departure stays hour 59.
Emergency: ship 7 North Wall Product (h80) is a priority discharge and should be berthed by hour 84, or a penalty of 20 per hour late to the berth applies (weight 3).
